title: DP-600: Implementing Analytics Solutions Using Microsoft Fabric
description: Practice exam covering Microsoft Fabric analytics solutions. Reflects the published DP-600 exam objectives.

scoring_guide.label: GOOD — Review missed domains and practice more.
NEEDS WORK — More hands-on practice recommended.

questions.text: You need to create a Fabric workspace that will be billed against your organization's Fabric capacity. Which workspace setting must you configure to link the workspace to that capacity?
questions.explanation: Workspaces must be assigned to a Fabric (or Premium) capacity to be billed against it and unlock Fabric workloads. This is done via the Workspace license mode / capacity assignment setting.

questions.text: Your organization wants developers to work on Fabric items using a branching workflow with pull requests, syncing changes back to workspaces. Which Fabric feature should you configure?
questions.explanation: Git integration connects a workspace to a Git repository (Azure DevOps/GitHub) enabling branching, commits, and pull requests.

questions.text: You are promoting a set of Fabric items (a lakehouse, notebooks, and a semantic model) from a Development workspace to a Test workspace, then to Production. Which feature is purpose-built for this?
questions.explanation: Deployment pipelines manage promotion of content across Development, Test, and Production stages.

questions.text: A workspace admin needs to grant a business analyst the ability to view and edit reports but NOT manage workspace settings or add members. Which workspace role should be assigned?
questions.explanation: Contributor can edit content but cannot manage workspace access or settings like Admin/Member can.

questions.text: You want to organize workspaces across the organization by business unit (e.g., Finance, Sales) for governance and discoverability purposes. Which Fabric feature should you use?
questions.explanation: Domains group workspaces by business area for governance, ownership, and discoverability.

questions.text: Which Fabric item type would you use to grant read access to a lakehouse's data to users who should not be able to modify pipelines or notebooks in the workspace?
questions.explanation: Viewer role grants read-only access to content without edit or management rights.

questions.text: You need to monitor capacity utilization across Fabric workloads (Power BI, Data Engineering, Data Warehouse) to identify throttling risk. Which tool should you use?
questions.explanation: The Fabric Capacity Metrics app provides visibility into capacity unit (CU) consumption and throttling across all Fabric workloads.

questions.text: An item in a workspace has been marked 'Certified.' What does this endorsement primarily signal to consumers?

options.text: The item is protected by sensitivity labels
The item has passed organizational quality/governance review
The item is automatically refreshed hourly
The item cannot be modified by anyone

questions.explanation: Certification indicates the item has been reviewed and approved by a governance authority in the organization.

questions.text: You need to store both structured (Delta tables) and unstructured (files) data in a single Fabric item that data engineers and data scientists can access through Spark. Which item should you create?
questions.explanation: A Lakehouse stores structured (Delta tables) and unstructured (files) data, accessible via Spark and a SQL analytics endpoint.

questions.text: You are building a data warehouse in Fabric and want to write T-SQL to create tables and load data. Which experience should you use?

options.text: Warehouse item with the SQL editor
Power Query Editor in Dataflow Gen2

questions.explanation: The Warehouse item provides a full read/write T-SQL experience.

questions.text: Which Fabric item allows low-code, Power Query-based transformation with the output automatically landing as Delta tables in OneLake?
questions.explanation: Dataflow Gen2 uses Power Query and outputs data as Delta tables in OneLake.

questions.text: You need to orchestrate a sequence of activities: copy data from an on-premises SQL Server, then run a notebook, then refresh a semantic model. Which Fabric item is best suited?
questions.explanation: Data pipelines orchestrate multi-step workflows across diverse activities including copy, notebook, and refresh operations.

questions.text: To connect to an on-premises SQL Server from Fabric, what must you install and configure?
questions.explanation: An on-premises data gateway is required to securely connect cloud services to on-premises data sources.

questions.text: What is a OneLake shortcut primarily used for?

options.text: Compressing Delta tables to reduce storage costs
Referencing data stored in another location (e.g., another lakehouse, ADLS Gen2, S3) without copying it
Creating a scheduled refresh for a dataflow
Assigning row-level security to a table

questions.explanation: Shortcuts are pointers to data in another location, avoiding data duplication.

questions.text: You want to ingest a continuous stream of IoT telemetry data and analyze it with near real-time queries. Which Fabric item is designed for this scenario?
questions.explanation: Eventstream ingests streaming data and can route it to a KQL Database for real-time analytical queries.

questions.text: In a medallion architecture implemented in a Fabric lakehouse, which layer typically contains raw, unaltered source data?
questions.explanation: Bronze is the raw ingestion layer; Silver is cleansed/conformed; Gold is business-level aggregated data.

questions.text: Which Spark language(s) can you use in a Fabric notebook to transform data in a lakehouse? (Select the BEST single answer)

options.text: All of the above (PySpark, Spark SQL, Scala, Spark R)

questions.explanation: Fabric notebooks support PySpark, Spark SQL, Scala, and SparkR — all four are available.

questions.text: You need to enforce that only rows where Region = 'West' are visible to a specific group of warehouse users. Which feature should you implement?
questions.explanation: Row-level security restricts which rows a user can query based on their identity or role.

questions.text: What is the primary difference between a Fabric Lakehouse and a Fabric Warehouse in terms of write access?

options.text: Lakehouses support only read access; warehouses support only write access
Lakehouses support both Spark and T-SQL reads (via SQL analytics endpoint, read-only) with Spark writes; warehouses support full T-SQL read/write

questions.explanation: Lakehouses expose a read-only SQL analytics endpoint alongside Spark read/write; Warehouses support full T-SQL read/write natively.

questions.text: You need to schedule a Dataflow Gen2 to refresh every night at 2 AM. Where do you configure this?

options.text: In the notebook's Spark session settings
In the dataflow's own scheduled refresh settings
In the workspace's Git integration settings
In the Fabric Capacity Metrics app

questions.explanation: Scheduled refresh is configured on the dataflow item itself.

questions.text: Which file format is the native storage format for tables in a Fabric Lakehouse?
questions.explanation: Delta format (Parquet files plus a transaction log) is the native lakehouse table format.

questions.text: You need to incrementally load only new or changed rows from a source table into your lakehouse rather than reloading all data each time. Which technique is most appropriate?

options.text: Full load with TRUNCATE and reload every run
Incremental refresh / watermark-based incremental load in the pipeline or dataflow

questions.explanation: Incremental/watermark-based loading avoids reprocessing unchanged data.

questions.text: A data engineer wants to optimize a large Delta table by compacting small files and improving read performance. Which command should they run in a notebook?
questions.explanation: OPTIMIZE (optionally with Z-ORDER) compacts files and improves query performance; VACUUM removes old files but doesn't compact.

questions.text: Which Fabric item would you use to write real-time queries against streaming telemetry using a SQL-like syntax optimized for time-series and log data?

options.text: KQL (Kusto Query Language) in a KQL Queryset

questions.explanation: KQL is purpose-built for querying time-series/log/telemetry data efficiently.

questions.text: You are designing a pipeline that must call a notebook conditionally based on the outcome of a prior activity. Which pipeline construct enables this?
questions.explanation: If Condition (or Switch) enables conditional branching logic in a pipeline.

questions.text: What is the purpose of the 'Copy data' activity in a Fabric data pipeline?

options.text: To move/copy data from a source to a destination, optionally with schema mapping
To copy a Power BI report between workspaces
To back up a semantic model

questions.explanation: Copy data activity moves data between a source and sink, with optional schema/column mapping.

questions.text: Which of the following is true about OneLake?

options.text: It is a separate storage account per workspace that must be manually provisioned
It is a single, unified, tenant-wide data lake built on ADLS Gen2 that all Fabric items store data in
It only stores Power BI datasets
It requires a separate Azure subscription

questions.explanation: OneLake is a single, tenant-wide lake (built on ADLS Gen2) shared across all Fabric workloads.

questions.text: You need to give a partner organization read access to specific Delta tables in your lakehouse without exporting or duplicating the data. What should you use?

options.text: External sharing / OneLake shortcuts to their tenant (where supported) or workspace sharing with appropriate permissions
Export to CSV and email the file

questions.explanation: External sharing capabilities (where enabled) or shortcuts let partners access specific data without duplication; exporting files is not the intended governed approach.

questions.text: What is the primary difference between Import mode and DirectQuery mode in a Power BI semantic model?

options.text: Import mode always queries the source live; DirectQuery caches data in memory
Import mode loads a compressed copy of the data into the model's memory; DirectQuery sends queries to the source at report run-time
DirectQuery only works with Excel files

questions.explanation: Import caches a compressed copy in memory for fast queries; DirectQuery executes queries against the source at run-time.

questions.text: Which storage mode combines Import and DirectQuery within a single semantic model, allowing some tables to be cached and others queried live?
questions.explanation: Composite/dual mode models combine Import and DirectQuery tables in one model.

questions.text: What is Direct Lake mode designed to do?

options.text: Cache data in a separate Azure SQL Database
Load data directly from Delta tables in OneLake into the semantic model's memory representation without a traditional import/refresh ETL step
Replace the need for a lakehouse entirely
Only work with on-premises data sources

questions.explanation: Direct Lake reads Delta tables directly from OneLake into memory for query, skipping a traditional import/refresh pipeline.

questions.text: You need to create a calculated column that concatenates FirstName and LastName in a semantic model. Which language should you use?
questions.explanation: DAX is the formula language used for calculated columns, measures, and calculated tables in semantic models.

questions.text: Which DAX function would you use to calculate a running total of Sales by date within the current filter context?

options.text: CALCULATE combined with a date filter (e.g., using FILTER and ALL/ALLSELECTED)

questions.explanation: A running total typically uses CALCULATE with a filter expression (e.g., dates <= current date) rather than SUM alone.

questions.text: You want to define a relationship between a Sales table and a Date table where one date row can relate to many sales rows. What cardinality should this relationship have?

options.text: One-to-many (one side on Date, many side on Sales)

questions.explanation: The 'one' side is Date, 'many' side is Sales — a standard one-to-many relationship in a star schema.

questions.text: What is the purpose of a star schema in semantic modeling?

options.text: To normalize all tables to reduce redundancy as much as possible
To organize data into fact tables (measures/events) and dimension tables (descriptive attributes) for optimized analytical querying
To store unstructured JSON data efficiently
To eliminate the need for relationships

questions.explanation: Star schema separates facts (measures) from dimensions (descriptive attributes) for efficient, intuitive analytical queries.

questions.text: You need to hide the technical key columns used only for relationships from report authors browsing the field list. What should you do?

options.text: Set the column's 'Is Hidden' property to true
Rename the columns to start with an underscore
Move them to a different table

questions.explanation: Setting 'Is Hidden' hides a field from the report field list while keeping it usable for relationships/calculations.

questions.text: Which feature allows you to define reusable, named business calculations (like 'Total Revenue' or 'YoY Growth') directly in the semantic model for consistent use across reports?
questions.explanation: Measures are reusable DAX calculations defined once in the model and reused across reports.

questions.text: You need to restrict report viewers so that a regional manager only sees data for their own region when viewing the same report as other managers. Which feature should you configure?

options.text: Row-level security (RLS) with DAX filter expressions tied to user identity

questions.explanation: RLS with DAX filter expressions (often tied to USERPRINCIPALNAME()) restricts visible rows per user.

questions.text: What is the benefit of enabling 'Large semantic model storage format' for a model approaching or exceeding 1 GB?

options.text: It removes the model size limitations associated with the default small dataset storage format, allowing larger models within capacity limits
It converts the model automatically to DirectQuery

questions.explanation: Large semantic model storage format removes the default size cap tied to small-model storage, subject to capacity limits.

questions.text: Which tool would you use to analyze and optimize the performance of DAX queries and identify expensive visuals or measures in a semantic model?

options.text: Performance Analyzer in Power BI Desktop

questions.explanation: Performance Analyzer in Power BI Desktop captures visual/DAX query durations to identify bottlenecks.

questions.text: You need to schedule automatic refresh of an Import-mode semantic model that pulls from a lakehouse. What must be true for scheduled refresh to succeed if the source requires credentials?

options.text: Nothing; scheduled refresh never requires credentials
Valid, configured data source credentials (and gateway, if needed) must be set for the semantic model
The model must be converted to Direct Lake
The workspace must be in Development mode

questions.explanation: Scheduled refresh requires valid configured credentials (and a gateway if the source is on-premises or requires one).

questions.text: What is a key advantage of Direct Lake mode over traditional Import mode for very large fact tables?

options.text: It requires no data at all
It avoids the need to fully import/refresh large volumes of data while still providing near-import-level query performance
It only works with CSV files
It eliminates the need for measures

questions.explanation: Direct Lake avoids a full import/refresh cycle for large data volumes while approaching Import-mode query speed.

questions.text: You want to quickly explore a lakehouse table's data distribution without writing code. Which Fabric feature allows this directly from the lakehouse UI?

options.text: Lakehouse 'Load to Tables' preview / SQL analytics endpoint query

questions.explanation: You can preview/query lakehouse table data directly via the UI or SQL analytics endpoint without external tools.

questions.text: A business user wants to ask natural-language questions like 'What were total sales last quarter?' against a semantic model without writing DAX. Which Power BI feature supports this?

options.text: Q&A visual / Copilot for Power BI

questions.explanation: The Q&A visual (and Copilot capabilities) let users ask natural-language questions against a semantic model.

questions.text: Which visual would be most appropriate to show the trend of monthly revenue over the past two years?
questions.explanation: A line chart is best suited to show trends over a continuous time period.

questions.text: You need to allow report consumers to dynamically switch between viewing Sales by Region vs. Sales by Product on the same visual. Which feature enables this?
questions.explanation: Field parameters let users dynamically swap the field(s) used in a visual, such as switching between Region and Product.

questions.text: What is the purpose of a Power BI dashboard versus a report?

options.text: A dashboard is a single-page, pinned-tile summary view often aggregating visuals from multiple reports; a report is a multi-page, interactive analytical document
A dashboard can only show one visual

questions.explanation: Dashboards are single-page pinned-tile summaries (often cross-report); reports are multi-page interactive documents built on a single dataset.

questions.text: You want business analysts to explore a semantic model's data in Excel using PivotTables connected live to the model. Which feature supports this?
questions.explanation: Analyze in Excel connects Excel PivotTables live to a published semantic model.

questions.text: Which DAX time intelligence function would you use to calculate year-to-date sales?
questions.explanation: TOTALYTD calculates a year-to-date aggregation directly; SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR and DATEADD shift periods rather than accumulate YTD.

questions.text: A stakeholder wants a single number showing current total sales, prominently displayed, with no axes or categories. Which visual type is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: The Card visual displays a single prominent value with no axes or categories.
